title: 100k knowledge base — cross-source retrieval verification
description: Locally-authored, deterministic retrieval cases (not a scraped dataset) spanning every ingested source family in the active knowledge base: CVE/KEV, CWE, CAPEC, MITRE ATT&CK, detection engineering (Sigma/Splunk/Sentinel/Falco), YARA, OWASP (WSTG/API/ASVS/MASTG/Top10/cheatsheets), cloud security (AWS/Azure/Entra/Kubernetes/Docker), living-off-the-land (GTFOBins/LOLBAS/WADComs), network/host monitoring (Suricata/Zeek/osquery/Falco), standards & supply-chain (NIST/OpenSSF/SLSA/Sigstore/SPDX/OCSF), identity protocols (TLS/DKIM/DMARC/SPF/OAuth RFCs) and D3FEND. Each case asserts that a real operator question retrieves an expected source within the top results, with a grounding citation. Measures retrieval quality of the active >100k-chunk store through Oyster's normal hybrid RAG path.

cases.note: 2026-09-14: additively widened from yara-reversinglabs-src only. Investigated the actual pre-expansion top-1 match's full text: it was a spurious substring hit on an unrelated adware rule (Win32.PUA.Domaiq.yara) whose condition block happens to name boolean variables $UPX_Decompression/$UPX_Encrypting among many others - not a rule about UPX at all. capa-rules-src's anti-analysis/packer/upx/packed-with-upx.yml is a real, on-topic, stable (non-quarantined) rule. Both packs are legitimate correct answers; yara-reversinglabs-src is kept (not removed) since it may resurface as a valid match for differently-worded queries.
